I read all of Basic.lean and the underlying lemmas in TauCeti/Algebra/Module/GradedModule/Multilinear/Basic.lean. Those lemmas are `coe_homogeneousMultilinearEquiv_apply` and `homogeneousMultilinearEquiv_symm_apply`, both tagged @[simp]. I also checked how Suspension.lean uses the file.

The file has two simp lemmas. `coe_pathOperationEquiv_apply` rewrites the coercion of the forward equivalence applied to `f d x` into `f.val` applied to the coerced inputs. `pathOperationEquiv_symm_apply` rewrites `.val` of the inverse on coerced inputs into the component `f d x`. Both rewrite toward the simpler, less structured side: the equivalence disappears and the raw value or component remains. The two LHS shapes are different, so they don't compete, and no rewrite cycle is possible. They mirror the underlying `InternalGrading` simp lemmas, which are both tagged @[simp] and whose first is proved by `rfl`.

Suspension.lean passes the underlying `InternalGrading.coe_homogeneousMultilinearEquiv_apply` to simp explicitly, not the local one. That is not evidence of a missing rule here, because the call goes through `InternalGrading.homogeneousMultilinearEquiv` directly. I found no missing canonical simp lemma, no wrong orientation and no unwanted expansion. The `abbrev` declarations are not simp-related issues. Unfolding `pathOperationEquiv` itself is not something simp should do.

I cannot run Lean, so I did not test simp behaviour and found nothing worth reporting.
